## Problem

All four `AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT` / `bound-exceeded` firings on 2026-08-12 missed the
`DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` bound by a hair: `deferred_for` = 1810s, 1820s, 1810s, 1930s against a
1800s bound — overshoots of 10s, 20s, 10s and 130s. Each one killed an in-flight LLM-Review
(the backfill reconciler retries it, but the gate stalls meanwhile), and they fired at ~10x
the normal rate during a 60+-merge landing burst. The bound is sized for a steady-state
review queue and is marginally too small for a burst; a bound that misses by 10s buys nothing
that a slightly larger bound would not have caught for free.

## Where it lives

- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:70-82` — the rationale comment + `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX="${DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX:-1800}"`.
  Commit 34cd pinned 1800s as **1.5x** `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (`DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS
  = 1200`, `src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:31`).
- `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py:399-420` —
  `test_defer_bound_default_outlasts_the_apps_own_per_review_cap` reads the shell default out of
  the script and asserts it against the app constant, so the two cannot drift. It currently pins
  the weaker `bound >= 1x` relationship.
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:133` — an alarm-cadence comment restating `1800s`.

## Decision

Raise the default to **2400s = 2.0x `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`**, and tighten the pinned test from
`>= 1x` to `>= 2x` so the new relationship is enforced rather than merely commented.

Why 2400 and not more: 2400s clears the worst observed overshoot (1930s) by 470s — ~3.6x the
130s miss — so all four firings would have deferred to completion. Why bounded at all: the
saturated-trace analysis on `greasy-plucky-piranha` showed that under *sustained* pipelining an
unbounded raise does not prevent the kill, it only defers it, while a deploy that never lands
is its own outage. Anchoring the bound to a fixed multiple of the app's own per-review cap keeps
it self-adjusting (raising `REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` drags the bound with it, enforced by the
test) instead of being a free-floating literal.

No terraform resource changes — the terraform edit here is comment-only, so nothing in this
ticket requires an operator apply.

## The counter-argument, and why the raise is still bounded

`greasy-plucky-piranha` (7b4a-0f39-1a45-4ce9) closed with an explicit "I would not raise the
bound". Its trace of the 03:03:04Z episode showed `in_flight` oscillating 2 -> 1 -> 2 and
**never reaching 0 across 30 continuous minutes**: no single review outlived
`REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, the bound was outlasted by ordinary *pipelining*. Under that
saturation a larger bound only defers the same kill. Tonight's sweep (`childsafe-bizarre-lorikeet`
b902-18af-14ed-4da1, comment 12) presents only the terminal markers, not per-episode `in_flight`
traces, so whether the four Aug-12 episodes were saturated the same way is **unestablished**.

This ticket therefore does not claim to fix saturated episodes. It claims the narrower thing the
data does support: four firings missed by 10-130s, and a bound at 2.0x rather than 1.5x the
per-review cap absorbs those margins. Where an episode really is saturated, 2400s defers the kill
by 600s and no more — which is precisely why the raise is a fixed multiple of the app's cap and
not an unbounded one. The underlying residue piranha carried forward (34cd's rationale treats a
*concurrent gauge* as if it were a single-review timer) is NOT closed by this ticket and remains
open on 7b4a's discovered_from chain.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q` — the pinned-relationship test and the
  full drain suite (the burst/bound scenarios drive the real script).
- `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` in `infra/terraform` (comment-only change, but the
  gates still run).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` default is `2400` in `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:82`, its rationale
      comment rewritten to state the 2.0x relationship and cite the 2026-08-12 overshoot data
      (1810/1820/1810/1930s against a 1800s bound). Checked: `grep DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX:- infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`.
- [x] `test_defer_bound_default_outlasts_the_apps_own_per_review_cap` asserts
      `bound >= 2 * DEFAULT_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` — updated deliberately, not deleted — with the
      docstring carrying the rationale. Checked:
      `pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q` passes.
- [x] The restated `1800s` figure in `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:133` reads 2400s.
      Checked: `terraform fmt -check` + `terraform validate` pass; no resource attribute changes,
      so `terraform plan` is a no-op and **no operator apply is required for this ticket**.
- [x] Change lands on `main` through Gerrit with `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
